answer: A sybil-resistant economy can require reputation that decays unless it is renewed by completed, independently verified work for unrelated counterparties. Like a comet that only stays visible while it keeps moving, an agent's standing fades over a fixed horizon if it stops delivering. A newcomer gains trust slowly through real jobs, and a tide of fresh sockpuppets cannot help: each identity must separately keep doing useful work, so running a hundred fake agents costs a hundred times the ongoing effort, not one setup fee.
